newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan stocks jump 6.0 pct on Bhutto's dismissal.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan stocks jump 6.0 pct on Bhutto's dismissal.

text.p: Pakistani stocks soared 6.01 percent on Wednesday on heavy buying triggered by the sacking of Benazir Bhutto's government.
By 0837 GMT, Karachi's 100-share index was up 87.00 points, or 5.80 percent, to 1,585.77 after briefly touching an intraday high of 1,607.84.

"People are bullish since the government was removed yesterday," dealer Khalid Waheed said. "Prices soared in Tuesday's kerb trading and that rally continues. But this sharp rise can prove dangerous because speculators dominate trading."
Wednesday's surge in Karachi's benchmark 100-index was the biggest one-day leap in the index this year, surpassing a 66.6-point rise on March 28, dealers said.
Bhutto was dismissed on Tuesday for a second time in her turbulent political career by president Farooq Leghari, who accused her beleaguered government of corruption, nepotism and misrule.
